subject.title: [Feature] Allow per-binding tool restrictions (tools.deny) in route/ACP bindings

question: Should OpenClaw add route/ACP binding `tools.allow` and `tools.deny` as a supported authorization boundary, or should operators use existing group, sender, session, and conversation policy surfaces instead?
rationale: This adds a public config and security-control surface whose precedence overlaps existing tool policy layers, so automation should not choose the permanent authorization model.

options.title: Design Binding Policy
options.body: Keep this open and approve an end-to-end binding policy contract with precedence, enforcement, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Use Existing Policy Surfaces
options.body: Decline the new binding key and document group/channel, sender, session, and per-agent policy as the supported tool restriction path.

options.title: Defer To Conversation Identity
options.body: Leave this blocked on broader scoped conversation identity/capability work if maintainers want one authorization model instead of a binding-specific slice.

recommendation.title: Design Binding Policy
recommendation.body: Keep this open and approve an end-to-end binding policy contract with precedence, enforcement, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the most recent scoped conversation capability work and have the strongest evidence-backed link to the cross-cutting policy decision.
